diagnosis.summary: Request rates on product-service, cart-service, and order-service have all risen approximately 3x from their baselines over the past 4 minutes. Latency has increased only slightly and 5xx error rates remain at zero across all three services. The stack appears to be absorbing the current load without meaningful degradation.
diagnosis.root_cause: A broad traffic spike across product-service, cart-service, and order-service is the most likely root cause.
evidence: product-service request_rate rose from 15.0 rps to 45.1 rps, a 3x increase.
cart-service request_rate rose from 2.0 rps to 6.0 rps, also a 3x increase.
order-service request_rate rose from 2.9 rps to 8.8 rps, approximately a 3x increase.
product-service p95_latency_ms rose from 24 ms to 31 ms and error_rate_5xx remains at 0.0, indicating no error degradation under the higher load.
order-service p95_latency_ms moved from 58 ms to 61 ms, a minor change with no sign of service stress.
recommended_actions: Check lambda_throttle_count on all three services to confirm the shared Lambda concurrency limit is not being approached as request rates remain elevated.
Monitor product-service db_consumed_read_capacity and read_throttle_events on the Products table, as the 3x traffic increase will proportionally raise read capacity consumption.
Determine whether the traffic increase is expected, such as a promotion or a client in a retry loop, before making any infrastructure changes.
If latency or error rates begin to rise, set rate and burst limits on the API Gateway stage to protect the stack while the traffic source is identified.
If lambda_throttle_count climbs, request a higher account concurrency quota or apply reserved concurrency to prevent one function from crowding out others.
